name: Citizenship by Naturalization

requirements.blocker_text: Constitution Article 24: Central American nationals may naturalize after just 1 year of residency, the shortest track available.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 1 year of residence in Honduras as a Central American national, then apply.

requirements.blocker_text: Constitution Article 24: Spanish and other Ibero-American nationals may naturalize after 2 consecutive years of residency.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 2 consecutive years of residence in Honduras as a Spanish or Ibero-American national, then apply.

requirements.blocker_text: Constitution Article 24: nationals of other countries may naturalize after more than 3 consecutive years of residency. All applicants under this and the regional tracks (except spouses -- see hn_citizenship_by_marriage.json) must renounce their previous nationality, unless a bilateral dual-nationality treaty applies.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate more than 3 consecutive years of residence in Honduras, then apply and renounce prior nationality unless a treaty exemption applies.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate / nationality document from home country

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 1 year (Central American), 2 years (Spanish/Ibero-American), or more than 3 years (other nationalities)

sources.title: Georgetown University Political Database of the Americas -- hosted text of Honduras's 1982 Constitution, Article 24 (naturalization tracks by nationality-of-origin, dual-nationality treaty rule)

BJ Abogados Honduras (private law-firm blog) -- Honduras's confirmed dual-nationality treaty with Spain (1966, Legislative Decree No. 60) and the de-facto US dual-nationality situation absent a treaty

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Honduras). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to an academic-hosted (Georgetown University) copy of the Constitution, tier 2, not a Honduran government domain directly; Honduras's own official gazette hosting was not located in this build. THE FULLER PICTURE on dual nationality (forward-referenced from hn_citizenship_by_descent.json's notes): Article 24 does NOT grant a universal right to dual nationality -- it applies 'when a double nationality treaty exists' between Honduras and the other country. Per a tier-4 law-firm source (not independently verified against a government text in this build), Honduras has a confirmed treaty with Spain (signed 1966, approved via Legislative Decree No. 60), letting Spaniards and Hondurans acquire the other's nationality without losing their own, subject to civil-registry dual-registration and military-service formalities. The same source states Honduras has no formal treaty with the US, but Hondurans naturalizing there can still end up dual because US law itself doesn't require renunciation -- a one-sided, treaty-independent outcome, not a Honduran-law guarantee. No other confirmed treaty partners were identified. GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE, QUANTIFIED FINDING: a three-tier residency ladder keyed to nationality-of-origin (1yr Central American / 2yr Spanish-Ibero-American / 3yr+ everyone else) is more granular than most naturalization tracks built elsewhere in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set true at the country-general level (treaty-dependent, not unconditional) -- this nuance is disclosed here rather than smoothed into a flat yes.
